transcript.text: The back burner on our gas hob has gone a lazy yellow colour and leaves black soot on the pan. What's wrong with it?

A lazy yellow flame that blackens pans is not normal: it means the gas is not burning cleanly. The usual cause is the burner cap/crown being greasy, wet, blocked or slightly out of position, which disrupts the air mix. If cleaning and correctly seating it makes no difference, the burner’s air/gas supply may need attention by a Gas Safe engineer. 1. Let the hob cool fully, switch it off and isolate it. Lift off the affected burner cap and the ring beneath it.
2. Wash off grease, food residue and any spill marks; make sure the small flame holes are clear without forcing or enlarging them. Dry both parts thoroughly.
3. Wipe the burner base and refit the ring and cap so they sit level and do not rock. Then light it normally. If the flame is now mainly crisp blue, the issue was seating/contamination. If it remains yellow, lazy or sooty after this, stop using that burner until a Gas Safe engineer checks it; do not try to adjust gas settings or dismantle the hob yourself. If other burners are also yellow or sooty, stop using the hob and arrange an urgent gas-supply/combustion check.
[Safety panel] If you can smell gas or think the appliance is unsafe, don't use it. Turn it off, open windows, and don't use switches or naked flames. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999, and have it checked by a Gas Safe registered engineer before using it again.
Thank you. I should mention that I've noticed a faint smell of gas near the hob a few times in the mornings, even when all the knobs are off. Should I still try cleaning the burner first?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
If you can smell gas, treat it as an emergency: don't turn any switches on or off and no naked flames. Turn the gas off at the meter if you safely can, open doors and windows, and leave if the smell is strong. Call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

candidates: Burner cap/crown dirty, wet or not seated squarely (high)
Blocked burner ports or air/gas mixture fault (medium)

plan: They asked: "What's wrong with it?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "Back burner has a lazy yellow flame and leaves black soot on pans". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
